summary: The No Aid for Ghost Students Act of 2026 requires the Department of Education to implement an identity fraud detection system to screen FAFSA applications starting October 1, 2026. If an application raises a reasonable suspicion of identity fraud, the Department must notify both the applicant and all designated colleges. Colleges are then prohibited from disbursing federal financial aid to those applicants unless the student's identity is verified through specific methods, such as in-person or live video checks, and the college notifies the Department of the successful verification.

affected_groups.effect: Must undergo additional identity verification (such as in-person or live video checks) before colleges can disburse federal financial aid.
affected_groups.group: FSA applicants flagged for suspected identity fraud

affected_groups.effect: Must check notices from the Department of Education, halt aid disbursement for flagged students until verified, use approved identity verification methods, notify the Department upon verification, and keep records.
Must screen all FAFSA forms for identity fraud, issue notices to applicants and schools, set institutional guidelines, and submit reports to Congress.

key_provisions: Requires the Department of Education to establish an identity fraud detection system to review every FAFSA application starting October 1, 2026.
Mandates that the Department notify applicants and designated colleges if an application presents a reasonable suspicion of identity fraud.
Prohibits colleges from disbursing federal financial aid to flagged applicants unless their identity is verified via in-person methods, live video, NIST IAL2 standards, or other approved means.
Requires colleges to maintain records of identity verifications and notify the Department once an applicant's identity is confirmed.
Directs the Department of Education to establish guidelines for institutional verification procedures and submit annual evaluations of the fraud detection system to Congress starting October 1, 2027.
Adds institutions that show a pattern of disbursing aid to flagged fraudulent applications to the Department's program review priority categories, unless they comply with verification rules.
missing_information: Specific funding amounts or costs associated with setting up and running the identity fraud detection system.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The No Aid for Ghost Students Act of 2026 requires the Department of Education to implement an identity fraud detection system to screen FAFSA applications starting October 1, 2026. If an application raises a reasonable suspicion of identity fraud, the Department must notify both the applicant and all designated colleges. Colleges are then prohibited from disbursing federal financial aid to those applicants unless the student's identity is verified through specific methods, such as in-person or live video checks, and the college notifies the Department of the successful verification.
summary_detail.significance: This bill establishes a nationwide, systematic verification protocol across the federal student aid application process to target potential identity fraud. It alters how colleges disburse financial aid by legally barring payouts to suspicious applicants until rigorous identity confirmation steps are completed, and creates congressional oversight and evaluation requirements for the Department of Education.
